answer.evidence: The flattening logic is in radon/visitors.py. ComplexityVisitor.blocks (around lines 198-207) builds the list from self.functions, then for each class appends the class and extends with cls.methods. Nested closures are collected in the function visitor path (around lines 274-292): a sub-visitor's functions are added to `closures`, and their complexity is deliberately not added to the parent (see #68). Inner classes are collected the same way in the class visitor (around lines 310-331). The review should check that qualified names are built consistently from the parent's name and that methods of inner classes keep the correct owning class. It should also check that blocks does not drop closures nested inside methods or inner classes of inner classes. Review time is split across the other candidates to check how they consume this block list. radon/raw.py and radon/metrics.py get the most time, to confirm that nothing there assumes a flat or top-level-only structure. radon/complexity.py gets a short pass over how it sorts and renders the blocks.
